result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.name: (Anti-)hypertriton lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE measured how long a rare, fragile nucleus called the hypertriton survives before decaying, using lead-lead collisions at the LHC. The collaboration reports a value compatible with representative theoretical predictions, contributing to the solution of a longstanding puzzle over this lifetime.

result:alice-hypertriton-lifetime-2019.title: ³ΛH and ³Λ̄H̄ lifetime measurement in Pb–Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV via two-body decay

result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.name: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV

summary.plain: ALICE measured how often J/psi particles (made of a charm quark and antiquark) survive lead-lead collisions at the LHC. The J/psi nuclear modification factor is larger than at the SPS and RHIC for the most central collisions, and models that produce J/psi from charm quarks in a deconfined phase can describe the data.

result:alice-jpsi-suppression-pbpb-2012.title: J/psi suppression at forward rapidity in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.key_value_text: Integrated yields of strange and multi-strange particles relative to pions increase significantly with event charged-particle multiplicity, reaching values similar to those seen in Pb-Pb collisions at the highest pp multiplicities.
result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.name: First observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions

summary.plain: ALICE found that the busier a proton-proton collision, the more strange particles it produces relative to pions, up to values similar to those in lead-lead collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma is formed. The paper presents this as the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.

result:alice-strangeness-enhancement-pp-.title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks
result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.significance: 5.4σ observed (5.5σ expected), combination of Run 1 and Run 2 H → bb̄ searches

summary.plain: ATLAS reports the observation of the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks, which the paper describes as the Standard Model Higgs boson's dominant decay (expected branching fraction about 58%). The main search looked for it produced together with a W or Z boson.

result:atlas-hbb-observation-2018.title: Observation of H -> bbbar decays and VH production with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.name: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.significance: 5.9σ (local); global significance about 5.1σ over the 110–600 GeV range

summary.plain: ATLAS reported a new particle with a measured mass of about 126 GeV, presented with CMS at a CERN seminar on 4 July 2012. The collaboration's title calls it 'a new particle' in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson; its abstract says the observation is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

result:atlas-higgs-observation-2012.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.key_value_text: Observation of H → ττ decays: 6.4σ observed (5.4σ expected) significance, 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data
result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons
result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.significance: 6.4σ observed (5.4σ expected), 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data

summary.plain: ATLAS reports an observation of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau leptons (heavier cousins of the electron), from 13 TeV data combined with earlier 7 and 8 TeV data. The paper reports cross-section measurements, all in agreement with Standard Model expectations.

result:atlas-htautau-observation-2018.title: Cross-section measurements of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau-leptons in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.name: Observation of light-by-light scattering in lead-lead collisions

summary.plain: ATLAS observed two photons (particles of light) scattering off each other, using the strong electromagnetic fields of lead nuclei that pass close to one another without touching; those fields act as a beam of nearly real photons.

result:atlas-lbyl-observation-2019.title: Observation of light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.name: A detailed map of Higgs boson interactions, ten years after the discovery

summary.plain: Ten years after the discovery, ATLAS combined an unprecedented number of Higgs boson production and decay measurements from its larger dataset to test how the particle interacts with others. The collaboration reports that the Higgs boson is remarkably consistent with the predictions of the theory.

result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022.title: A detailed map of Higgs boson interactions by the ATLAS experiment ten years after the discovery

key_value.display: 2.30 TeV (95% CL exclusion, massless lightest neutralino)

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.name: Exclusion limits on squarks and gluinos from the full Run 2 dataset

summary.plain: ATLAS searched its full second run of LHC data for the supersymmetric partners of quarks and gluons (squarks and gluinos) and found no statistically significant deviation from the expected background. It set a 95% confidence-level limit: in a simplified model with only a gluino and a massless lightest neutralino, gluino masses up to 2.30 TeV (trillion electronvolts) are excluded.

result:atlas-squark-gluino-limit-2020.title: Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with jets and missing transverse momentum using 139 fb^-1 of sqrt(s)=13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.name: Measurement of the top quark mass

summary.plain: ATLAS measured the mass of the top quark, one of the fundamental particles of the Standard Model, using 8 TeV collision data, and combined the result with its earlier top-quark mass measurements.

result:atlas-topmass-measurement-2018.title: Measurement of the top quark mass in the ttbar -> lepton+jets channel from sqrt(s)=8 TeV ATLAS data and combination with previous results

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.name: Observation of Higgs boson production in association with a top quark pair

summary.plain: ATLAS observed Higgs bosons being produced together with a top quark and its antiparticle, which the paper describes as a more direct test of the Higgs boson's coupling to the top quark, the heaviest particle in the Standard Model.

result:atlas-tth-observation-2018.title: Observation of Higgs boson production in association with a top quark pair at the LHC with the ATLAS detector

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.name: Measurement of the W boson mass

summary.plain: ATLAS measured the mass of the W boson, a carrier of the weak force, from 7 TeV collision data recorded in 2011 (7.8 million W→μν and 5.9 million W→eν candidates), obtaining 80370 ± 19 MeV.

result:atlas-wmass-measurement-2017.title: Measurement of the W-boson mass in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=7 TeV with the ATLAS detector

result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.name: Evidence for the purely leptonic decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅

summary.plain: Belle presented the first evidence that a B particle can decay straight into a tau lepton and a neutrino. Because a neutrino cannot be seen, events were selected by fully reconstructing one of the two B particles produced in each collision.

result:belle-b-to-tau-nu-evidence-2006.title: Evidence of the Purely Leptonic Decay B⁻ → τ⁻ ν̅_τ

result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.name: Observation of large CP violation in the neutral B meson system
result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.significance: more than 6σ (a zero value of sin 2φ₁ is ruled out)

summary.plain: Belle measured how the decay-time distributions of neutral B particles and their antiparticles differ for certain final states, and found a large asymmetry (sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14 ± 0.06). The collaboration concluded that it had observed CP violation, a matter–antimatter asymmetry, in the neutral B meson system, and ruled out a zero value at more than 6σ.

result:belle-cp-violation-observation-20.title: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

summary.plain: Belle reports evidence that a neutral D particle can turn into its own antiparticle ('mixing') before it decays, seen as a small difference in apparent lifetime between two kinds of D decay. The paper says its value is more than 3σ from zero, whereas earlier measurements averaged about 2σ above zero.

result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.name: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅ decays

summary.plain: Belle II reports the first evidence for a very rare B decay into a kaon and two neutrinos. Because the neutrinos leave no trace, the analysis uses the properties of the accompanying B meson in each collision. The paper says the combined result is 2.7 standard deviations above the Standard Model expectation.

result:belle-ii-b-to-k-nunu-evidence-202.title: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ ν ν̅ decays

result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.name: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass

summary.plain: Belle II measured the mass of the tau lepton, one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model, and states in its abstract that the result is the most precise to date.

result:belle-ii-tau-mass-measurement-202.title: Measurement of the τ-lepton mass with the Belle II experiment

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.name: Determination of |Vcb| using B→Dℓνℓ Decays at Belle II

summary.plain: Belle II measured how often a B meson (a particle containing a bottom quark) decays into a D meson plus a lepton and neutrino, and used that to determine |Vcb|, a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model that determines how often bottom quarks turn into charm quarks.

result:belle-ii-vcb-measurement-2025.title: Determination of |Vcb| using B→Dℓνℓ Decays at Belle II

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.name: Observation of the X(3872)

summary.plain: Belle reported observing a narrow new state, the X(3872), in B-meson decays to π⁺π⁻J/ψ. Its mass is very near the D⁰D̄*⁰ threshold; the paper says the mass and the absence of a strong signal in a related decay channel are in some disagreement with expectations for one charmonium state, and calls it suggestive of a loosely bound molecule.

result:belle-x3872-observation-2003.title: Observation of a narrow charmonium-like state in exclusive B± → K± π⁺π⁻ J/ψ decays

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.key_value_text: Excess of a few counts per day per 100 t of target attributed to CNO-neutrino interactions
result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.name: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun
result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.significance: stated only as 'high statistical significance'; the abstract gives no σ value

summary.plain: Borexino reports the direct observation, with high statistical significance, of neutrinos from the Sun's secondary fusion cycle (the CNO cycle), which the collaboration calls the first experimental evidence of this process. The abstract says the process is dominant in the energy production of massive stars.

result:borexino-cno-evidence-2020.title: Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun

result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.key_value_text: pp neutrino interaction rate 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst) counts per day per 100 t
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.name: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun
result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.significance: 10σ (absence of pp solar neutrinos excluded; statistical significance)

summary.plain: Borexino reported spectral observations of the Sun's most abundant neutrinos, the pp neutrinos from the very first step of the fusion chain that powers it, which the paper says had hitherto eluded direct detection.

result:borexino-pp-first-detection-2014.title: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.key_value_text: Top quark mass 176 ± 8 (stat) ± 10 (sys) GeV/c²; t t̄ production cross section 6.8 +3.6/−2.4 pb
result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.name: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab

summary.plain: In March 1995 the CDF experiment announced its observation of top-quark production in proton–antiproton collisions at Fermilab's Tevatron. The paper reports a signal inconsistent with the background prediction by 4.8σ and a top-quark mass of 176 ± 8 (stat) ± 10 (syst) GeV/c². Fermilab describes the top quark as the last undiscovered quark of the six predicted by current theory.

result:cdf-top-quark-observation-1995.title: Observation of Top Quark Production in ppbar Collisions with the Collider Detector at Fermilab

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.name: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV

summary.plain: CMS reported an excess of events above background near 125 GeV that, in its words, signals the production of a new particle, at a joint CERN seminar on 4 July 2012. The paper gives a mass of 125.3 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.5 (syst) GeV and says the two-photon decay indicates a boson with spin different from one.

result:cms-higgs-boson-observation-2012.title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.name: A portrait of the Higgs boson ten years after the discovery

summary.plain: Ten years after the discovery, CMS reported what it calls the most up-to-date combination of its results on the Higgs boson's properties (decays, spin-parity, mass and production), together with a limit on Higgs boson pair production. The collaboration says that, within the uncertainties, all these observations are compatible with the Standard Model.

result:cms-higgs-boson-portrait-2022.title: A portrait of the Higgs boson by the CMS experiment ten years after the discovery

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.name: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks
result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.significance: 5.6σ observed (5.5σ expected), combination with H → bb̄ searches in other production processes

summary.plain: CMS reports the observation of the Higgs boson decaying to bottom quarks, which the paper calls the most prevalent decay mode (predicted branching fraction about 58%). The main contribution comes from events where the Higgs boson is produced together with a W or Z boson.

result:cms-higgs-to-bb-observation-2018.title: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to tau leptons
result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.significance: 5.9σ observed (5.9σ expected), 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data

summary.plain: CMS reports the first observation of Higgs boson decays to tau leptons by a single experiment, from 13 TeV data combined with earlier 7 and 8 TeV data (observed significance 5.9 standard deviations). Tau leptons are heavy relatives of the electron.

result:cms-higgs-to-tau-tau-observation-.title: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons with the CMS detector

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.name: Search for new high-mass dilepton resonances and nonresonant phenomena (2016–2018 data)

summary.plain: CMS searched its 2016–2018 13 TeV data (up to 140 fb^-1) for electron or muon pairs from a heavy new particle and saw no significant deviation from the Standard Model background. The abstract says the limits are the most stringent to date on the masses of various spin-1 particles, spin-2 gravitons (Randall–Sundrum model) and spin-1 dark-matter mediators.

result:cms-high-mass-dilepton-search-202.title: Search for resonant and nonresonant new phenomena in high-mass dilepton final states at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

aliases: Observation of the rare decay Bs0 -> mu+ mu- (CMS and LHCb combined)
result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.name: Observation of the rare decay B⁰ₛ → μ⁺μ⁻ (CMS and LHCb combined)

summary.plain: CMS and LHCb combined their 2011–2012 data to make the first observation of a B_s meson decaying into two muons, a decay the Standard Model predicts to be very rare: about four in every billion B_s mesons produced.

result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2.title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.name: Observation of long-range near-side angular correlations in pp collisions ("the ridge")

summary.plain: CMS reported the first observation, in proton-proton or proton-antiproton collisions, of a long-range 'near-side' correlation: in high-multiplicity 7 TeV collisions, pairs of particles are emitted in nearly the same azimuthal direction while far apart in pseudorapidity (angle relative to the beam).

result:cms-long-range-near-side-correlat.title: Observation of Long-Range Near-Side Angular Correlations in Proton-Proton Collisions at the LHC

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.name: Measurement of the top quark mass: 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the top quark, which its paper calls the most massive fundamental particle, as 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV from 13 TeV collision data; the abstract says the approach significantly improves the precision over previous measurements.

result:cms-top-quark-mass-measurement-20.title: Measurement of the top quark mass using a profile likelihood approach with the lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV

summary.plain: CMS observed Higgs bosons produced together with a top quark and an anti-top quark. The paper explains that on-shell top quarks are too heavy to appear in Higgs boson decays, so this production process is how the Higgs boson's coupling to the top quark can be constrained.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.name: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the W boson, which the collaboration calls the best-precision measurement of the W mass at the LHC, and found it in agreement with the Standard Model prediction. The paper notes that a measurement by the CDF collaboration at the Tevatron disagrees strongly with both the Standard Model expectation and the other measurements.

result:cms-w-boson-mass-measurement-2024.title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.name: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon
result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.significance: more than 3σ (two independent analyses, against the background-only hypothesis)

summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first measurement of neutrinos scattering coherently off argon nuclei, using a 24-kilogram liquid-argon detector at Oak Ridge. The rate is consistent with the Standard Model; together with the earlier caesium-iodide result, the collaboration says it confirms the existence of the process.

result:coherent-argon-measurement-2021.title: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.key_value_text: Weak mixing angle sin^2(theta_W) = 0.220 (+0.028/-0.026) at Q^2 ~ (50 MeV)^2, alongside constraints on non-standard interactions and a test of lepton flavor universality using the neutrino beam's timing structure
result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.name: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT

summary.plain: COHERENT re-measured the rate of neutrinos scattering coherently off caesium-iodide nuclei with more than twice the data of the first observation and a better model of nuclear recoils in the crystal. The collaboration calls it the most precise measurement of the process yet, and extracts the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer near 50 MeV.

result:coherent-csi-cross-section-2022.title: Measurement of the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Cross Section on CsI by COHERENT

result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.name: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array

summary.plain: COHERENT reports the first detection of neutrinos scattering coherently off natural germanium, using an array of eight high-purity germanium detectors at Oak Ridge. The collaboration calls the result evidence: it rejects the no-scattering hypothesis at 3.9σ, and the signal rate agrees with the Standard Model within 2σ.

result:coherent-germanium-evidence-2024.title: Evidence of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering with COHERENT's Germanium Array

result:coherent-observation-2017.name: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering

summary.plain: COHERENT reports observing neutrinos scatter off entire atomic nuclei at once, a process the paper says had evaded experimental demonstration for forty-three years after its first theoretical description. The detector was a 14.6-kilogram caesium-iodide crystal at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge.

result:coherent-observation-2017.title: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering

result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.key_value_text: 17 candidate events observed against an expected background of 3.8+/-0.6; probability of a background fluctuation 2.0e-6 (4.6 standard deviations)
result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.name: Observation of the Top Quark

summary.plain: On 2 March 1995 the D0 experiment at Fermilab's Tevatron and the CDF experiment announced the top quark together. D0's paper reports 17 events against an expected background of 3.8, concludes that D0 has observed the top quark, and measures its mass and production rate.

result:d0-top-quark-observation-1995.title: Observation of the Top Quark

result:daya-bay-observation-2012.key_value_text: far-hall observed/expected ratio R = 0.940 ± 0.011(stat) ± 0.004(syst); non-zero θ13 with a significance of 5.2σ
result:daya-bay-observation-2012.name: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

summary.plain: Daya Bay measured a non-zero value of the neutrino mixing angle θ13, with a significance of 5.2σ. It compared antineutrinos from six nuclear reactors in detectors at near and far sites: fewer arrived at the far site, about 1.6 kilometres away, than expected without oscillation.

result:daya-bay-observation-2012.title: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

result:donut-tau-neutrino-observation-20.key_value_text: Evidence of four tau neutrino interactions against an estimated background of 0.34 events
result:donut-tau-neutrino-observation-20.name: Observation of tau neutrino interactions

summary.plain: On 21 July 2000 the DONUT collaboration announced at Fermilab what the laboratory called the first direct evidence for the tau neutrino. In 203 neutrino interactions recorded in nuclear emulsion, a decay search found evidence of four tau neutrino interactions against an estimated background of 0.34 events; the abstract adds that this number is consistent with the Standard Model expectation.

result:donut-tau-neutrino-observation-20.title: Observation of tau neutrino interactions

result:double-chooz-evidence-2012.name: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment

summary.plain: Double Chooz's detector, 1.05 kilometres from the Chooz reactors in France, saw fewer reactor antineutrinos than expected if the mixing angle θ13 were zero: 8,249 events against 8,937 expected. The collaboration interprets the deficit as evidence of electron antineutrino disappearance.

result:double-chooz-evidence-2012.title: Reactor electron antineutrino disappearance in the Double Chooz experiment

result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.name: Excavation of the DUNE far-site caverns completed at SURF

summary.plain: Workers finished excavating the three caverns, about a mile underground in South Dakota, that will house DUNE's giant detectors. Fermilab said outfitting of the caverns would begin soon, followed by installation of the detectors.

result:dune-far-site-excavation-2024.title: Excavation of colossal caverns for Fermilab's DUNE experiment completed

result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.name: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP single-phase LArTPC performance in a beam test

summary.plain: ProtoDUNE-SP is a prototype of DUNE's first far-detector module, built with full-size components and tested in a particle beam at CERN. The paper reports measured values that meet or exceed the DUNE far-detector specifications, and says its successful operation demonstrates the effectiveness of the single-phase far-detector design.

result:dune-protodune-sp-performance-202.title: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform

result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.name: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

summary.plain: The Homestake chlorine detector had been measuring solar neutrinos since 1970; this paper reports the combined result of 108 extractions, a solar-neutrino-induced argon-37 production rate of 2.56 SNU. In his Nobel lecture Raymond Davis Jr. summarises the outcome as the Sun producing one-third as many neutrinos as expected: the solar neutrino problem.

result:homestake-flux-measurement-1998.title: Measurement of the Solar Electron Neutrino Flux with the Homestake Chlorine Detector

result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.key_value_text: No new physics signal observed in a search for long-lived particles from kaon decay that decay to two muons, with NuMI-beam data corresponding to 2.41×10²⁰ protons-on-target; the paper reports "world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches"
result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.name: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS

summary.plain: ICARUS searched for a hidden-sector particle that could be produced in kaon decays and then decay into two muons inside the detector. It saw no signal and set limits; the paper describes them as world-leading for heavy QCD axions and, among dedicated searches, for the Higgs portal scalar.

result:icarus-hidden-sector-scalar-limit.title: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.name: Atmospheric neutrino mixing measurement with IceCube DeepCore

summary.plain: IceCube's DeepCore sub-array measured how atmospheric neutrinos change type on their way through the Earth, using 2011–2019 data with improved calibration. The collaboration says the 40% error reduction makes this the most precise measurement of oscillation parameters using atmospheric neutrinos, and that the results are compatible and complementary to those from accelerator beams.

result:icecube-deepcore-atmospheric-osci.title: Measurement of Atmospheric Neutrino Mixing with Improved IceCube DeepCore Calibration and Data Processing

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.key_value_text: 28 events, purely atmospheric origin rejected at 4σ
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.name: Evidence for high-energy extraterrestrial neutrinos
result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.significance: 4σ (purely atmospheric origin rejected, both searches combined)

summary.plain: IceCube reported 28 high-energy neutrino events that interact inside the detector. The collaboration says a purely atmospheric origin is rejected for these events at the 4σ level, and that their properties are consistent with generic predictions for an additional component of extraterrestrial origin.

result:icecube-evidence-extraterrestrial.title: Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.name: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

summary.plain: Using machine learning on ten years of data, IceCube identified neutrino emission from the plane of our own Milky Way at the 4.5σ level of significance. The signal is consistent with modelled diffuse emission from the Galactic plane, but could also arise from a population of unresolved point sources.

result:icecube-galactic-plane-neutrinos-.title: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.name: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance

summary.plain: IceCube detected a single particle shower with an energy of about 6 PeV (six thousand trillion electronvolts) that is consistent with being created at the Glashow resonance: the resonant formation of a W⁻ boson when a high-energy electron antineutrino meets an electron.

result:icecube-glashow-resonance-candida.title: Detection of a particle shower at the Glashow resonance with IceCube

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.name: Evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068

summary.plain: IceCube found an excess of about 79 neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068, at a significance of 4.2σ. The collaboration interprets it as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy, and says the inferred neutrino flux exceeds the potential TeV gamma-ray flux by at least one order of magnitude.

result:icecube-ngc-1068-evidence-2022.title: Evidence for neutrino emission from the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.key_value_text: Best fit sin²(2θ₂₄) = 0.10, Δm²₄₁ = 4.5 eV²; consistent with no sterile neutrino, p = 8.0%
result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.name: eV-scale sterile neutrino search with eight years of atmospheric muon neutrinos

summary.plain: IceCube searched eight years of atmospheric muon-neutrino data for a fourth, 'sterile' kind of neutrino that would distort how atmospheric neutrinos pass through the Earth. The best-fit point is consistent with no sterile neutrino (p-value 8.0%).

result:icecube-sterile-neutrino-search-2.title: An eV-scale sterile neutrino search using eight years of atmospheric muon neutrino data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.name: Multimessenger observation of blazar TXS 0506+056 with IceCube-170922A

summary.plain: On 22 September 2017 IceCube detected a neutrino of about 290 TeV whose arrival direction was consistent with a known gamma-ray blazar, TXS 0506+056, that was observed to be in a flaring state. Telescopes from radio waves to gamma rays followed up, and the collaboration says the coincidence suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-multimesseng.title: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A

result:icecube-txs-0506-056-prior-neutri.title: Neutrino emission from the direction of the blazar TXS 0506+056 prior to the IceCube-170922A alert

result:kamiokande-sn1987a-1987.title: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A

result:kamland-first-results-2002.title: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

result:katrin-neutrino-mass-upper-limit-.title: Direct neutrino-mass measurement based on 259 days of KATRIN data

The paper says the event's energy is much larger than that of any neutrino detected so far.

result:km3net-uhe-neutrino-observation-2.title: Observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino with KM3NeT

result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.key_value_text: The abstract says the mass and width of the Z boson and its couplings to fermions are precisely measured, and that the number of light neutrino species is determined to be 2.9840 ± 0.0082; it reports electroweak radiative corrections beyond the running of the QED and QCD couplings observed with a significance of five standard deviations, and the largest difference from the Standard Model expectation among Z-pole measurements, the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry, at 2.8 standard deviations.

The paper reports that the largest difference from the Standard Model expectation among the Z-pole measurements is 2.8 standard deviations, in the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry.

result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006.title: Precision Electroweak Measurements on the Z Resonance

result:lep-higgs-exclusion-2003.title: Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson at LEP

result:lep-three-neutrino-species-1989.title: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species

result:lhcb-cp-violation-charm-observati.name: Observation of CP violation in charm decays

summary.plain: LHCb found that charm particles and their antimatter partners decay in measurably different ways: the first observation of this matter-antimatter difference (CP violation) in the decay of charm hadrons. The same kind of difference had already been established for kaons and B mesons.

result:lhcb-cp-violation-charm-observati.title: Observation of CP Violation in Charm Decays

result:lhcb-doubly-charmed-baryon-observ.title: Observation of the Doubly Charmed Baryon Ξcc++

result:lsnd-antineutrino-appearance-evid.title: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam

result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.name: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure

result:lux-complete-exposure-2016.title: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure

result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.name: First results from the LUX dark matter experiment at the Sanford Underground Research Facility

The authors say the data disagree with low-mass dark matter interpretations of several other experiments' results, and that the limit is a significant improvement over earlier searches' sensitivities.

result:lux-first-wimp-search-2013.title: First results from the LUX dark matter experiment at the Sanford Underground Research Facility

result:lz-first-wimp-search-2022.title: First Dark Matter Search Results from the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

result:lz-ws2024-wimp-search-2024.title: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

result:meg-mu-to-e-gamma-limit-2016.title: Search for the Lepton Flavour Violating Decay mu+ -> e+ gamma with the Full Dataset of the MEG Experiment
